answer: Each agent can post a bond that is slashed if its actions are proven fraudulent, while rewards accrue gradually as independent peers verify useful work. Creating many identities does not multiply influence for free: every identity needs its own locked capital, and coordinated accounts can lose those bonds together when evidence links their claims. The terrace may widen participation, but the kernel is one costly stake per identity; attackers must tie up funds and risk losing them across the canyon of verification.
